'''Jūnisho Jinja''' (十二所神社), also referred to as '''Jūnisha Jinja''' (十二社神社), '''Jūni Hashira Jinja''' (十二柱神社), or '''Jūni Tenjin Jinja''' (十二天神社), are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines|1=Shinto shrine}} found throughout {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. Some of these shrines are also called '''Jūnishō''' (十二社). 

These shrines can be categorized into two main types:
1. Shrines dedicated to local mountain deities called '''Jūni-sama''' (Twelve Lords), associated with ancient rituals and the customs of the "Twelve Lectures." These shrines are primarily found in mountainous areas of eastern Japan, especially in the northern {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kantō region|1=Kantō region}} and {{ill|Kōshin'etsu region|en|Kōshin'etsu region|qid=Q398208|lt=Kōshin'etsu region|1=Kōshin'etsu region}}. Research indicates that 65% of the 438 shrines named Jūnisho or Jūnisha enshrine {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}} as their main deity.
2. Shrines that enshrine the {{ill|Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Sanzan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} deities (known as {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen}}). These were originally called '''Jūnisho Gongen-sha'''. During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, many of these shrines modified their enshrined deities to the "{{ill|Heavenly Generations Seven|ja|天神七代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heavenly Generations Seven|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神世七代|1=Kamiyonanayo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3275893}}" and "{{ill|Earthly Generations Five|ja|地神五代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Generations Five|1=Five Generations of Earth Deities|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18337308}}," or the "Twelve Gods of the Heavenly Generation."
